extra.text: The new if (object == null) return undefined; runs before the typeof criterion === 'function' branch, so function criteria are never called for null/undefined elements. Lodash's baseOrderBy calls the function on every element, including null ones. For example, orderBy([null, {a:2}, {a:1}], [o => o ? o.a : -1]) should put null first (key -1), but now its key is undefined and it goes last. Move the null check below the function branch so it only applies to key/path criteria, and add a spec case for a function criterion with null elements, since no test covers this now.

Because of the count bug, the existing tests that pass a function or property iteratee fail against the committed code, and so do the new shorthand and nullish-iteratee tests. The committed change can't pass CI as it is. Fix line 139, then run yarn vitest run src/compat/array/intersectionBy before merging.

extra.text: The ternary is backwards. count = hasIteratee ? values.length : values.length - 1 counts the iteratee as if it were one of the arrays to intersect. Take intersectionBy([2.1, 1.2], [2.3, 3.4], Math.floor): the loop reaches Math.floor, sees it isn't array-like, and returns []. The string shorthand 'x', null, numbers and objects all fail the same way, and so does the single-array uniqBy path. When there's no iteratee, the last array is skipped instead, so intersectionBy([1, 2], [2], [3]) returns [2] rather than []. Running yarn vitest run src/compat/array/intersectionBy gives 14 failed and 8 passed, including the new tests. Use const count = hasIteratee ? values.length - 1 : values.length;.

This undefined iteratee test can't catch the bug above. It expects [], and the broken code already returns []. It also passes with or without the identity fallback. Use inputs that share a value, e.g. intersectionBy([2.1, 1.2], [2.1, 3.4], undefined) expecting [2.1].
